# L03: Easing: why animations look robotic

Unnamed (Ugoki motion course promo) · upload ·  · notes: [lessons/03_easing-motion-curves.md](../../brain/lessons/03_easing-motion-curves.md)

**Core lesson:** Entrances ease out, exits ease in, interface elements spring with slight overshoot, and nothing moves linearly.


## Ideas from this source (10)

- **[Claim plus instant visual proof](../topics/hooks.md#hook-bold-claim-visual-proof)** · hooks: Back the opening claim with proof on screen in the first 2–3 s: L01 pairs "scientifically impossible to skip" with a retention graph; L03 shows ROBOT vs PRO animations side by side.
- **[Question on a pain point](../topics/hooks.md#hook-pain-question)** · hooks: Open with a question about the viewer's pain: "Does your animation look robotic?", "Why do your Claude edits look pro but sound like a silent movie?". Caleb calls a thought-provoking question a "thumbs stopper".
- **[Entrances ease out, exits ease in](../topics/effects.md#fx-ease-out-entrances)** · effects: Things that arrive ease out (fast, then a long brake, "as if set down by a steady hand"); things that leave ease in (slow start, then away). Oren's overlays slide in with spring/ease-out.
- **[UI and text pops: spring with slight overshoot](../topics/effects.md#fx-spring-ui)** · effects: Interface elements and text pops use a spring that overshoots its target a little, then settles (spring/bounce slide-ins in L02; spring UI cards in L07).
- **[Nothing linear](../topics/effects.md#fx-nothing-linear)** · effects: Nothing in the real world moves at constant speed; linear motion starts and stops all at once and looks robotic.
- **[Khandala pans and push-ins were linear](../topics/effects.md#fx-khandala-linear-moves)** · effects: Khandala animates its photos with slow pans and push-ins (sun to subject, cliff + cactus), but our ffmpeg build moved them at constant speed (linear), the opposite of L03's rule.
- **[Make motion visible with a dotted trail](../topics/effects.md#fx-trail-visual-proof)** · effects: The easing tutorial has no cuts: a position-vs-time graph animates continuously with a dotted trail (evenly spaced = linear, bunched = eased) while caption words change every ~0.3–0.5 s.
- **[Word-by-word captions, key word highlighted](../topics/text.md#text-word-by-word-highlight)** · text: One word or phrase at a time; the key word sits in a coloured highlight box (red box in L03, yellow or a selection box in Rahul's Layout A).
- **[Near-black with one accent colour](../topics/colour.md#colour-near-black-one-accent)** · colour: The easing tutorial is near-black with a red glow, red as the only accent; Rahul uses yellow (≈ #F5B800) on black as his single brand accent everywhere.
